summary: Year One, Semester One of Wheaton Press's Becoming a Disciple middle school Bible sequence (Year One stresses belonging, with essential questions on understanding and loving God's Word). Cast as archaeologists on a journey through Chicago, London, Paris, Israel, Greece and Rome, students collect artifacts for a virtual museum. Along the way they weigh whether the Bible is trustworthy and trace its plot and several recurring 'threads' toward the 'golden thread' that ties Scripture together. The publisher calls it an introduction to a relational, missional God rather than a Bible survey.

toc.label: Unit One
toc.title: How do I understand the Bible?
toc.covers: Probably how to read and evaluate the Bible: its languages, literary forms, and archaeological, geographical and historical setting, which the publisher lists as the course's lenses.

toc.label: Unit Two
toc.title: What is the Plot of the Bible?
toc.covers: The overall storyline of Scripture as one unfolding narrative of God's mission.

toc.label: Unit Three
toc.title: What is the Purple thread?
toc.covers: One of the color-coded recurring motifs traced through Scripture; the page does not say what purple stands for (in biblical imagery purple is often tied to royalty and kingship).

toc.label: Unit Four
toc.title: What is the Scarlett thread?
toc.covers: A second color-coded motif; the page does not define it (a 'scarlet thread' usually names the theme of blood, sacrifice and redemption running through Scripture).

toc.label: Unit Five
toc.title: What is the Blue thread?
toc.covers: A third color-coded motif; the page does not define it (blue in the tabernacle and Israel's tassels is often read as pointing to heaven and God's commands).

notes: The work list's 'Engaging the Heart' is Wheaton Press's series brand; the book is the first middle school guide in that line. The unit headings come from a 2018 publisher catalog page, which may predate the 2019 printing, so check them against the copy in hand. 'Scarlett' is spelled that way on the catalog page. No lesson-level contents, sample pages or author credit were found. The product page says students examine 'four significant motifs' while the catalog lists three colored threads plus the golden thread, so the motif count may differ in the printed book. The course is paired with an online component (Engaged Schools LMS), and the second-semester guide is 'True Hero' (ISBN 978-1-950258-15-4).
